Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can get you an apples-to-apples pricing estimate:

- Acme expected traffic: 2M API requests/month for the customer support assistant (avg session = 8 turns). You mentioned average prompt length ~700 characters and average model response ~1,200 characters.
- Budget signal: you said leadership is targeting ~$1,200 per month initially for the MVP but can expand if unit economics look good.
- Open items for us to confirm: how you want us to report usage (tokens vs characters vs requests), whether prompt caching applies to your workflow, and what target $/1M tokens would make sense for you.

Two quick asks: can you drop the usage estimates spreadsheet from today (numbers you showed) into the Drive link I shared? I attached a worksheet template (acme_usage_estimates.xlsx) to this thread for our model.

Separately, I know there was some confusion on metrics — I wanted to clarify the differences so the numbers we send are interpretable by your finance team:
- Tokens vs characters: our billing is per billed token. Tokens roughly correspond to ~3-4 characters in English on average, but it varies by language and punctuation.
- Requests: these are API calls (1 request can include multiple prompts/turns depending on how you batch). Billing is driven by tokens consumed by the model (input + output) — not by request count.
- Prompt caching: if you have repeated identical prompts (e.g., templated system messages or identical user messages), we can apply prefix caching to reduce inference work. Caching reduces compute and therefore billed tokens only if the runtime can serve responses from cache (and the cache match avoids model decoding). Important: caching does not change the definition of a token — it reduces billed compute in some cases but we still record the token-equivalent for traceability.

I'll put together a short worked example that converts your char estimates to tokens and shows cost at different $/1M token tiers. Rishi + Priyom, can you confirm the assumptions I should use for token-to-character ratio and caching effectiveness?

Thanks —

Great — thanks for uploading the sheet, Alex. Below is the simple worked example Rishi and I discussed; I'll attach a populated tab in the workbook as well.

Worked example (averages):
- Assumptions: 1 token ≈ 4 characters (conservative for English); average request = input 700 chars + output 1,200 chars = 1,900 chars total -> ≈ 475 tokens per request.
- If you have 2M requests/month -> 2,000,000 * 475 = 950,000,000 tokens/month (950M tokens).
- Cost tiers: at $20 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost = (950M / 1M) * $20 = $19,000/month. At $15 / 1M tokens -> $14,250/month.

Prompt caching and billing nuance:
- Prefix/prompt caching example: assume 30% of your input prompts are templated system messages or identical queries (e.g., standard customer metadata) and can be cached. If caching eliminates the need to re-run the full prompt and the model can return a cached response, you reduce compute.
- Important billing note: we bill on billed tokens consumed by inference. If a cached response avoids decoding tokens entirely, you do not incur (or incur reduced) billed tokens for that request. However, partial caching (only prefix cached) still requires some decoding for the variable portion; billed tokens will reflect the actual compute.
- In practice, effective billed tokens reduction depends on how often cache hits happen and whether the cache covers most of the heavy input (long system messages). We'll run a small pilot to measure hit rate before projecting savings.

Because your target budget for MVP is ~$1,200/mo for API spend, the current estimates (~$14k-$19k at $15-$20/1M) are well above that. Two levers to hit your budget range:
1) Reduce token consumption per request (shorter responses/prompts, templating, response truncation).
2) Aggressive caching of repeated prompts (pilot to measure hit rate).
3) Negotiate committed volume pricing / dedicated capacity (Reserved capacity can significantly reduce $/1M tokens for predictable workloads).

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi / Priyom: please populate the attached workbook tab with a conservative token ratio (we used 1 token = 4 chars) and an optimistic ratio (1 token = 3 chars) and include a caching-hit scenario (0%, 20%, 40%).
- Alex: after you review those scenarios, tell us what trade-offs you'd be comfortable with (response length limits, more templating) and whether you want us to model a reserved capacity option at 6 or 12 month commit.
